en grævling.explanation: "En grævling" means "a badger". To name the home it digs in the ground, use "en grævlingegrav" (a badger sett): "Vi fandt en grævlingegrav i skoven" (We found a badger sett in the forest).

en grønlænder.explanation: "En grønlænder" means "a Greenlander". Greenland, "Grønland", is part of the Danish Realm. To name the language, use "grønlandsk" (Greenlandic): "Bogen er skrevet på grønlandsk" (The book is written in Greenlandic).

en grønthandler.explanation: "En grønthandler" means "a greengrocer". It is built from "grønt" (vegetables) and "en handler" (a dealer). To talk about the shop, the same word is used: "Jeg går hen til grønthandleren" (I am going over to the greengrocer's).

en grøntsag.explanation: "En grøntsag" means "a vegetable". It is built from "grønt" (greens) and "en sag" (a thing). To say you eat vegetables, say: "Jeg spiser grøntsager hver dag" (I eat vegetables every day).

en gud.explanation: "En gud" means "a god". To talk about the one God, say "Gud" without "en": "Tror du på Gud?" (Do you believe in God?)

en gudfar.explanation: "En gudfar" means "a godfather". It is built from "gud" (god) and "far" (father). To say whose godfather he is, use "til" (to): "Han er gudfar til min søn" (He is godfather to my son).

en gudmor.explanation: "En gudmor" means "a godmother". It is built from "gud" (god) and "mor" (mother). To say whose godmother she is, use "til" (to): "Hun er gudmor til min datter" (She is godmother to my daughter).

en guide.explanation: "En guide" means "a guide". To say a tour has a guide, use "guidet" (guided): "Vi tager på en guidet tur" (We go on a guided tour).

en guidebog.explanation: "En guidebog" means "a guidebook". It is built from "en guide" (a guide) and "en bog" (a book). To name the place a guidebook covers, use "til" (to): "en guidebog til København" (a guidebook to Copenhagen).

en guirlande.explanation: "En guirlande" means "a garland". The spelling "guirlande" has "ui" after the "g". To say you hang garlands up, use "hænge op" (hang up): "Vi hænger guirlander op til festen" (We hang garlands up for the party).

en guitar.explanation: "En guitar" means "a guitar". To say an electric one, put "el-" in front: "en elguitar" (an electric guitar).

en guldfisk.explanation: "En guldfisk" means "a goldfish". It is built from "guld" (gold) and "fisk" (fish). The plural stays "guldfisk": "to guldfisk" (two goldfish).

en guldsmed.explanation: "En guldsmed" means "a dragonfly". When you talk about a person who works with gold, the same word means "a goldsmith": "Ringen er lavet af en guldsmed" (The ring was made by a goldsmith).

en gulerod.explanation: "En gulerod" means "a carrot". It is built from "gul" (yellow) and "rod" (root), so it is literally "a yellow root". In the plural the vowel changes: "gulerødder" (carrots), as in "Jeg køber tre gulerødder" (I buy three carrots).

en gulvvask.explanation: "En gulvvask" means "a floor washing". It is built from "gulv" (floor) and "vask" (washing), so both "v" letters stay in the spelling. To say you wash the floor, use the verb: "Jeg vasker gulv hver lørdag" (I wash the floor every Saturday).

en gummistøvle.explanation: "En gummistøvle" means "a rubber boot". It is built from "gummi" (rubber) and "en støvle" (a boot). To say a pair, use "et par" (a pair of): "et par gummistøvler" (a pair of rubber boots).

en gut.explanation: "En gut" means "a guy / lad". It is an informal word. To greet a group of friends, say: "Hej, gutter!" (Hi, guys!)

en guvernør.explanation: "En guvernør" means "a governor". To say which place the governor leads, use "i" (in): "guvernøren i Californien" (the governor of California).

en gyde.explanation: "En gyde" means "an alley". To say you walk through an alley, use "gennem" (through): "Vi går gennem gyden" (We walk through the alley).

en gymnastiksal.explanation: "En gymnastiksal" means "a school gym". It is built from "gymnastik" (gymnastics) and "en sal" (a hall). The part "sal" is also in "en festsal" (a banquet hall).

en gynge.explanation: "En gynge" means "a swing", as at a playground. To say a child is swinging, use the verb "at gynge" (to swing): "Barnet gynger" (The child is swinging).

en gåde.explanation: "En gåde" means "a riddle / mystery". To say you solve a riddle by guessing, use "gætte" (guess): "Kan du gætte gåden?" (Can you guess the riddle?) When nobody can explain something, the same word means "a mystery": "Det er en gåde, hvorfor hun forsvandt" (It is a mystery why she disappeared).

en gågade.explanation: "En gågade" means "a pedestrian street". It is built from "gå" (walk) and "en gade" (a street). Strøget in Copenhagen is a famous one.

en gård.explanation: "En gård" means "a farm, a courtyard". When you talk about the shared yard behind an apartment building, the same word means "a courtyard": "Børnene leger i gården" (The children play in the courtyard).

en gårdhave.explanation: "En gårdhave" means "a courtyard garden". It is built from "gård" (courtyard) and "have" (garden). The first part, "gård", also means "a farm": "Vi bor på en gård" (We live on a farm).
